_metadata.independence: I read only u07-blind-input.json; no other file, repository search, web lookup or external API was used.

hints.reason: RING is reached as a near-synonym (a ring is a circle); BAT only via the loose verb image of bats circling overhead, which few players would land on.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; RING side is solid but the BAT side is a weak verb image.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The one hint is essentially a RING synonym with a thin BAT attachment.

hints.reason: BAT via echolocation (bat sonar is a schoolbook fact); ROBOT via sonar/ultrasonic sensors that robots and robot vacuums navigate with.

best_available.why: A shared sensing idea that genuinely reaches both words; robot side is a step less automatic than the bat side.

pairs.pair_note: Single hint, passes on a shared 'navigates by sonar' route.

hints.reason: BAT via bats roosting in caves; ROCK via a cave being a hollow in rock with rock walls and formations.
BAT via the famous story of Ozzy Osbourne biting the head off a bat on stage; ROCK via Ozzy as a rock star.

best_available.why: Broadest and most immediate for both words; OZZY is an equally strong single-story hint but skews to older or rock-aware players.

pairs.pair_note: Two good hints with different flavours: one scene (cave), one story (Ozzy).

hints.reason: ROSE via its thorns; BAT has no route at all to THORN.
BAT via vampire bats drinking blood; ROSE only via the colour phrase 'blood-red rose', a mood/colour link.

best_available.why: Reaches BAT strongly and ROSE via a familiar colour phrase; the only hint with any two-sidedness.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. THORN is wholly one-sided; BLOOD leans on a colour route for ROSE.

hints.reason: BAT via bats roosting in caves; SALT via salt caves and salt mines (salt-cave therapy, Wieliczka), a recognised compound.

best_available.why: Bat side is automatic; 'salt cave' is a real, moderately familiar phrase that lets players reach SALT.

pairs.pair_note: Passes on the strength of 'salt cave' as a compound; a second opinion on how familiar that phrase is would be reasonable.

hints.reason: BAT via the iconic bat silhouette (Batman emblem, Halloween cut-outs); SHADOW via silhouette as a dark outline, near-synonym.
BAT via the Bat-Signal; SHADOW only because the Bat-Signal is a bat shadow projected onto the clouds, which players must reason out.

best_available.why: Both words land immediately; the bat silhouette is one of the most recognisable outlines there is.

pairs.pair_note: SILHOUETTE is excellent; SIGNAL is a clever Batman route whose SHADOW side needs a reasoning step.

hints.reason: BAT via the vampire-bat bite; SHARK via the shark bite, both everyday fears.

best_available.why: Clean two-sided hint on the animals' most famous action.

pairs.pair_note: Single strong hint.

hints.reason: SNAKE via snake venom; BAT fails because bats are not venomous (vampire bats bite but inject no venom).
BAT via vampire-bat fangs (and the vampire image); SNAKE via snake fangs.

best_available.why: Both animals are defined by fangs in the popular imagination.

pairs.pair_note: FANGS passes cleanly; VENOM rests on a false fact about bats.

hints.reason: SPRING via 'spring training' as a compound; BAT via that same scene being baseball batting practice.

best_available.why: One shared baseball scene reaches both words; mainly a North American phrase but very familiar there.

pairs.pair_note: Strong single hint via the spring-training compound.

hints.reason: BAT via bats as nocturnal night flyers; STAR via stars appearing in the night sky.
BAT via the baseball bat; STAR via a baseball star or All-Star game, a familiar but secondary sense.

best_available.why: Both words are among the first things anyone associates with night.

pairs.pair_note: Two passes; NIGHT is the stronger and fairer.

hints.reason: TRAIN via trains running through tunnels; BAT via bats roosting in dark tunnels (disused railway tunnels are classic bat roosts).

best_available.why: A shared dark-passage setting that both words naturally occupy.

pairs.pair_note: Strong single hint.

hints.reason: WATER via skimming stones or skimming the water's surface; BAT via bats skimming low over water to drink or catch insects, a true but little-known behaviour.

best_available.why: Only hint; WATER is reached easily but the bat behaviour is a naturalist's fact rather than common knowledge.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The bat side is accurate but obscure.

hints.reason: WITCH via the witch's broomstick; BAT has no route to BROOM beyond sharing Halloween decor with it.
BAT and WITCH are both stock Halloween icons; one shared scene reaches both directly.

best_available.why: Both words are first-tier Halloween imagery.

pairs.pair_note: HALLOWEEN is excellent; BROOM is a witch-only attribute.

hints.reason: BAT via vampire-bat fangs; WOLF via the wolf's bared fangs.
BAT via the vampire turning into a bat; WOLF via Dracula's wolf form and the vampire-versus-werewolf lore of Dracula and Twilight.

best_available.why: A single story world (Dracula) that contains both the bat and the wolf; FANGS is equally fair but more generic.

pairs.pair_note: Two strong hints; VAMPIRE is the more specific shared story.

hints.reason: BEAR via teddy bear; BELL has no route to TEDDY.
BEAR via hiking in bear country; BELL via the bear bell hikers wear to warn bears off, a scene known mainly to outdoors people.

best_available.why: The bear-bell hiking scene genuinely joins both words, but only hikers will see the BELL side quickly.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. HIKING is a real shared scene and could be promoted if the owner judges bear bells familiar enough.

hints.reason: BRIDGE via a bridge crossing; BEAR via the 'Bear Crossing' road sign and bears crossing roads and rivers.

best_available.why: Bridge side is automatic and the wildlife-crossing sign gives BEAR a fair, recognisable route.

pairs.pair_note: Passes; the bear side is the secondary one.

hints.reason: CARD via the 'wild card' compound; BEAR via bears as wild animals ('wild bear').

best_available.why: Both routes are ordinary usage; the bear side is generic but fair.

pairs.pair_note: Single fair hint.

hints.reason: BEAR via Pixar's Brave, where Merida's mother is turned into a bear; CASTLE via the Scottish castle of DunBroch where the film is set.

best_available.why: One well-known film carries both words, in the spirit of the POISON/Snow White anchor; players who miss the film get nothing.

pairs.pair_note: Passes as a shared story; worth a second opinion on whether the bear transformation in Brave is widely remembered.

hints.reason: BEAR via bear paws; CAT via cat paws, both everyday.
BEAR via bear claws (also the pastry); CAT via a cat's retractable claws.

best_available.why: Slightly more distinctive than PAWS, which also fits dogs and rabbits; both are fully two-sided.

pairs.pair_note: Two clean passes.

hints.reason: BEAR via Paddington Bear; CROWN via Paddington's tea with the Queen for the Platinum Jubilee and the Paddington tributes after her death, a largely British memory.

best_available.why: Only hint; the royal link is real and affectionate but not what most players carry for Paddington.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The crown side depends on the 2022 Jubilee sketch.

hints.reason: BEAR via the black bear; DIAMOND via black diamonds (the ski-run grade, the gem, the brand), both standard compounds.

best_available.why: Two established compounds, not a mood colour.

pairs.pair_note: Single strong hint.

hints.reason: DOG via hound as a synonym; BEAR only via bear-hunting hounds (Plott hound, Karelian Bear Dog), which few players know.
BEAR via thick bear fur; DOG via dog fur, both immediate even if the hint is broad.

best_available.why: Plain and two-sided; generic is not a defect under the rubric.

pairs.pair_note: FUR passes; HOUND is mostly a DOG synonym.

hints.reason: BEAR via the giant panda as China's bear; DRAGON via the Chinese dragon as the national symbol.
BEAR via the panda being a bear; DRAGON via Kung Fu Panda, where Po becomes the Dragon Warrior.

best_available.why: Geography reaches both symbols without needing a film plot.

pairs.pair_note: CHINA is the safer pass; PANDA passes on Kung Fu Panda's Dragon Warrior and deserves a second look.

hints.reason: EGG via the Easter egg hunt; BEAR via the bear hunt (the picture book 'We're Going on a Bear Hunt' and bear hunting).

best_available.why: Two familiar compounds that share the same word.

pairs.pair_note: Single strong hint.

hints.reason: FIRE via campfire; BEAR via bears raiding campsites, the classic camping worry.
BEAR via Smokey Bear; FIRE via his 'only you can prevent wildfires' message and the smoke itself.

best_available.why: A single character who is both a bear and a fire mascot; CAMP is nearly as good and more international.

pairs.pair_note: Two strong hints; SMOKEY is mainly a US reference.

hints.reason: FISH via the catch of the day; BEAR via the bear catching fish mid-leap, a familiar nature image though less automatic as a word link.
FISH via salmon being a fish; BEAR via grizzlies catching salmon at the falls.

best_available.why: The bear-at-the-salmon-run scene is iconic and salmon is unmistakably a fish.

pairs.pair_note: Two passes; SALMON is the stronger.

hints.reason: GHOST via spirit as a synonym; BEAR via the spirit bear (Kermode) or the bear as a spirit animal, both a stretch for a general player.

best_available.why: Only hint; the bear side exists (spirit bear, spirit animal) but is not what SPIRIT evokes.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Essentially a GHOST synonym.

hints.reason: GLASS via the glass jar; BEAR via Winnie the Pooh's head in the honey jar and gummy bears in a jar.

best_available.why: Material route for GLASS and a famous story scene for BEAR.

pairs.pair_note: Single strong hint.

hints.reason: BEAR via Goldilocks and the Three Bears; GOLD via her golden locks, but the hint literally contains the target GOLD, which most hint rules forbid.
BEAR via the grizzly on the California Bear Flag (and Cal's Golden Bears); GOLD via the Gold Rush and the Golden State.

best_available.why: Geography reaches both words strongly without embedding the target; GOLDILOCKS is a better story link but contains GOLD.

pairs.pair_note: GOLDILOCKS is held at BORDERLINE purely on the contains-target flag; if the owner allows containment it is a top-tier hint.

hints.reason: BEAR via the bear hug; HEART only via hugs as a gesture of love, a mood association rather than a scene or phrase.
BEAR via the Care Bears; HEART via the heart badges on the Care Bears' tummies and 'caring heart', which players must reconstruct.

best_available.why: Bear hug is universal and hug-to-heart is an easy emotional step, though not a definite route.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Both hints reach BEAR via a compound and HEART only via feeling.

hints.reason: HORSE via wild horses (the phrase and the song); BEAR via bears as wild animals.

best_available.why: Both are wild animals and 'wild horses' is a set phrase.

pairs.pair_note: Single fair hint.

hints.reason: BEAR via the caged circus or zoo bear; IRON via the iron cage, the material cages are made of.

best_available.why: A single object that both words naturally attach to.

pairs.pair_note: Single strong hint.

hints.reason: KEY via the wind-up key; BEAR via the wind-up toy bear, which exists but is not the first wind-up toy players picture.

best_available.why: Only hint; the wind-up toy scene is coherent but the bear is incidental to it.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Bear side is weak.

hints.reason: BEAR via Baloo in The Jungle Book; KING via King Louie in the same story and 'king of the jungle'.

best_available.why: One story holds both a bear and a king, with the generic 'king of the jungle' as backup.

pairs.pair_note: Strong single hint.

hints.reason: KNIGHT via a knight's armour; BEAR only via the armoured bears of His Dark Materials, which most players will not reach.

best_available.why: Only hint; functionally one-sided for anyone who has not read Pullman.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Close to a FAIL; kept BORDERLINE because the bear route is real.

hints.reason: LIGHT via the Northern Lights; BEAR via the polar bear of the far north and the Great Bear in the northern sky, neither a set phrase.

best_available.why: The Arctic scene (aurora over polar bears) is familiar, but BEAR has no compound with NORTHERN.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS, but a plausible shared Arctic scene; a reasonable owner could promote it.

hints.reason: BEAR and LION are both headline zoo animals.
LION via the Cowardly Lion of The Wizard of Oz; BEAR via the famous chant 'lions and tigers and bears, oh my!'.

best_available.why: A single story line names both animals; ZOO is fine but fits many animals.

pairs.pair_note: Two passes.

hints.reason: MOON via the moon in the sky; BEAR via the Great Bear (Ursa Major, the Big Dipper's constellation) in the night sky.

best_available.why: Constellation route is a recognised path, comparable to the BROOKLYN/Big Apple anchor, though the bear side takes a step.

pairs.pair_note: Passes narrowly; worth a second opinion on how readily players reach BEAR from SKY.

hints.reason: BEAR via bear fur; MOUSE via its soft fur, both plain and two-sided.

best_available.why: Broad but reaches both words directly.

pairs.pair_note: Single generic pass.

hints.reason: BEAR via polar bear; NIGHT via the 'polar night' of the Arctic winter, a real term that many players will not know.

best_available.why: Only hint; bear side is immediate and polar night is a genuine compound, just not a common one.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Hinges on familiarity with 'polar night'.
